rejected_rule.statement: Courts may give a broad construction to deeds when the true intention of the parties is manifest, even if there is an error in the written instrument.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: "I find, however. that this is precisely what was done by Bertram C.J. and Sampayo J. in Fernando v. Fernando 2[(1921) 23 N. L. R. 483.]. The facts of that case require to be closely examined. ... It Is important to note that Sampayo J. who wrote the judgment in Bernard v. Fernando, agreed with Bertram J.'s ruling in the later case."
